learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Electrographic Seizure Patterns.
Apply Electrographic Seizure Patterns to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Electrographic seizures typically show evolution in frequency, morphology, amplitude or spatial distribution.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Rhythmic artifact and benign patterns can imitate seizures. Critical-care criteria use standardised terminology and clinical correlation.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Recognising evolution helps separate ictal activity from rhythmic artifact.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Calling any rhythmic activity a seizure leads to harmful overtreatment.

reviewPrompts.answer: Rhythmic artifact and benign patterns can imitate seizures. Critical-care criteria use standardised terminology and clinical correlation.
Recognising evolution helps separate ictal activity from rhythmic artifact.
Calling any rhythmic activity a seizure leads to harmful overtreatment.
Evolution and context are stronger than rhythm alone.
